title: 📘 UNIT 1: DEVELOPMENT OF CAPITALISM AND NATIONALISM (1815–1914)
notes: This unit examines the development of capitalism, the Industrial Revolution, nationalism and the unification of Italy and Germany.

title: 1.1 💰 Development of Capitalism
notes:
Capitalism → economic system based mainly on private ownership, profit, competition and market exchange.

Mercantilism → system in which merchants bought goods cheaply and sold them at higher prices for profit.

Capitalism developed from the decline of feudalism and expanded through trade, capital accumulation and investment in production.

Industrial capitalism → emerged in the 18th century with factory production and investment in machinery.

Main features:
• Private ownership of property.
• Profit motive.
• Free competition.
• Wage labor.
• Market-based production.
• Capital accumulation.

Laissez-faire → limited government interference in economic activity.

title: 1.1.1 📊 Marxian Economics
notes:
Karl Marx analyzed capitalism in terms of class relations and exploitation.

Main ideas:
• Society is divided into social classes.
• Bourgeoisie → owners of the means of production.
• Proletariat → wage workers who sell their labor.
• Class conflict → struggle between opposing economic classes.
• Surplus value → value produced by workers beyond the wages they receive.

Marx predicted that class conflict would eventually lead to major social and economic transformation.

title: 1.2 🏭 The Industrial Revolution
notes:
Industrial Revolution → transition from hand production and small-scale manufacturing to machine production and factories.

It began in Britain in the 18th century and later spread to other parts of Europe and the world.

Major factors:
• Agricultural improvements.
• Availability of coal and iron.
• Capital accumulation.
• Growing population and labor supply.
• Expanding markets.
• Scientific and technological innovations.
• Improved transportation.

title: 1.2.1 ⚙️ Major Industrial Innovations
notes:
Important developments included:

• Steam engine → provided mechanical power for industry and transport.

• Spinning Jenny → increased textile production.

• Power loom → mechanized weaving.

• Cotton gin → increased cotton processing.

• Iron and steel production → supported machines, railways and construction.

• Railways → transformed transportation and markets.

📌 Factory production increased productivity and lowered production costs.

title: 1.2.2 🌍 Effects of the Industrial Revolution
notes:
Economic effects:
• Growth of factories and industries.
• Expansion of capitalism.
• Increased production and trade.
• Development of banking and transportation.

Social effects:
• Rapid urbanization.
• Growth of the industrial working class.
• Expansion of the middle class.
• Poor working and living conditions for many workers.
• Child and female labor.

Political effects:
• Growth of labor movements.
• Expansion of political and social reform movements.
• Increased competition for overseas markets and resources.

title: 1.3 🏳️ Nationalism
notes:
Nationalism → belief that people sharing a common identity should have political unity and self-government.

Factors promoting nationalism:
• Common language and culture.
• Shared history and traditions.
• Popular education and literacy.
• Printing and newspapers.
• Romanticism.
• Opposition to foreign rule.
• Growth of nation-states.
• French Revolution and its ideas of citizenship and national sovereignty.

Nationalism contributed strongly to the unification of Italy and Germany.

title: 1.3.1 🧠 Nationalism and Imperialism
notes:
Nationalism encouraged European states to compete for political power and international prestige.

Imperialism → policy of extending a state's political, economic or military control over other territories.

Economic motives → search for raw materials, markets and investment opportunities.

Political motives → national prestige, strategic interests and competition among European powers.

Social and ideological motives → missionary activities, racial theories and Social Darwinism.

title: 1.4 🇮🇹 Unification of Italy
notes:
Before unification, Italy was divided into several states, with Austria controlling or influencing parts of northern Italy.

Major obstacles:
• Political division.
• Austrian influence.
• Weak national consciousness in some areas.

Key figures:

• Giuseppe Mazzini → promoted republican nationalism.

• Count Cavour → led diplomatic and political unification from Piedmont.

• Giuseppe Garibaldi → led military campaigns in southern Italy.

• Victor Emmanuel II → king around whom unified Italy developed.

Key events:
• 1859 → Piedmont and France defeated Austria; Lombardy was gained.
• 1860 → Garibaldi captured Sicily and Naples.
• 1861 → Kingdom of Italy proclaimed.
• 1866 → Venetia joined Italy.
• 1870 → Rome became part of Italy; unification was completed.

title: 1.5 🇩🇪 Unification of Germany
notes:
Germany was divided into many states before unification. Prussia became the leading force.

Key figure:
• Otto von Bismarck → Prussian statesman who used diplomacy and war to unify Germany.

Bismarck's policy → Realpolitik, emphasizing practical political interests and power.

Major wars:
• Danish War (1864) → Prussia and Austria defeated Denmark.
• Austro-Prussian War (1866) → Prussia defeated Austria.
• Franco-Prussian War (1870–71) → Prussia and its German allies defeated France.

1871 → German Empire proclaimed at Versailles; Wilhelm I became German Emperor.

📌 Germany was unified mainly under Prussian leadership.

title: 1.6 🇺🇸 The American Civil War
notes:
The American Civil War (1861–1865) was fought mainly between the Union (North) and Confederacy (South).

Major causes:
• Slavery.
• Conflict over its expansion into new territories.
• Economic differences between North and South.
• States' rights and federal authority.
• Political conflict over slavery.

Abraham Lincoln → President of the Union during the war.

1863 → Emancipation Proclamation declared enslaved people in rebel-held territories free.

1865 → Confederacy defeated; slavery and secession were decisively rejected.

title: 1.6.1 ✊ Results of the American Civil War
notes:
• Union preserved.
• Slavery abolished through the 13th Amendment.
• 14th Amendment → citizenship and equal protection under law.
• 15th Amendment → voting rights for African American men.
• Federal government became stronger.
• Southern economy and society were severely disrupted.
• Reconstruction followed the war.

📌 Abraham Lincoln was assassinated shortly after the Confederate surrender in April 1865.

title: 1.7 🌍 The Eastern Question
notes:
Eastern Question → the problem of what would happen to Ottoman territories as the Ottoman Empire declined, especially in the Balkans.

Main factors:
• Decline of Ottoman power.
• Rise of Balkan nationalism.
• Russian expansion and support for some Slavic peoples.
• Rivalry among European great powers.
• Strategic and economic interests in Ottoman territories.

📌 The decline of the Ottoman Empire created competition among Russia, Austria-Hungary, Britain and other European powers.

title: 1.7.1 ⚔️ The Balkan Wars
notes:
First Balkan War (1912–1913) → Balkan League states fought the Ottoman Empire and captured most of its European territories.

Second Balkan War (1913) → Bulgaria fought former allies over territorial gains; Bulgaria was defeated.

Results:
• Ottoman territory in Europe greatly reduced.
• Balkan states expanded.
• Rivalries among Balkan states increased.
• Serbia became stronger.
• Tensions among European powers increased.

📌 Balkan nationalism and great-power rivalry contributed to the unstable conditions that preceded World War I.

title: 🏆 UNIT 1 — MUST REMEMBER
notes:
💰 Capitalism → private ownership + profit + competition + wage labor.
🏭 Industrial Revolution → machine production + factories + urbanization.
🏳️ Nationalism → national unity + self-government.
🇮🇹 Italy → Mazzini + Cavour + Garibaldi + Victor Emmanuel II → unification by 1870.
🇩🇪 Germany → Bismarck + Prussia + three major wars → German Empire, 1871.
🇺🇸 Civil War → slavery + states' rights + sectional conflict → Union victory and abolition of slavery.
🌍 Eastern Question → decline of Ottoman Empire + Balkan nationalism + European rivalry.
⚔️ Balkan Wars → 1912–1913 → Ottoman losses + increased Balkan and European tensions.

🧠 EXAM TIP:
Remember the major unification figures:
Italy → Mazzini, Cavour, Garibaldi, Victor Emmanuel II.
Germany → Bismarck, Wilhelm I.

Remember the sequence:
Capitalism → Industrial Revolution → Nationalism → Unification → Imperialism → Great-power rivalry.
